model: probability-weighted scenario model on forward EV/Sales (NOT a discounted-FCF model)
valuation_philosophy: Rua straddles the 'distressed' and 'operating company' rows of the dcf-methods routing table. It is a going concern with real, fast-growing revenue (H1 FY2026 NZ$1.334m, +92% YoY) and shrinking burn, so a receivership/creditor waterfall is wrong. But it has never produced positive free cash flow in any period on record (owner FCF FY2025 -NZ$2.83m), so an owner-FCF DCF has no positive flow to discount and Gordon math on negative flows produces a meaningless runaway-negative number. Book-value/NTA anchors are also out: PwC issued a DISCLAIMER OF OPINION on both FY2024 and FY2025 accounts, citing inability to corroborate going concern and the recoverability of ~NZ$5.3m of goodwill/PP&E/held-for-sale assets - the printed NZ$5.845m equity is not audit-assured, and verified-tangible equity is closer to ~NZ$2.8m (equity less NZ$2.195m goodwill less the NZ$0.861m held-for-sale facility the auditor could not sign off). The model used instead: three scenarios valued on a forward (FY2028) EV/Sales multiple appropriate to a sub-scale, unprofitable, going-concern-qualified distributor, each with scenario-specific dilution explicitly modelled (every raise at a NZ$0.035 tick-floor price is enormously dilutive), discounted 2 years at a 28% NZD cost of equity. Insolvency is priced as an explicit 60%-weighted branch inside a 40%-weighted bear scenario - NOT in the discount rate - so it is charged exactly once. The weighted IV of NZ$0.0145 sits ~59% BELOW the current NZ$0.035 price: the market is currently paying 4.3x annualised run-rate sales, above even this model's 2.5x bull-case exit multiple. That is the finding, stated plainly - the current price requires the bull case (UK deal converts, Germany/Australia hold, zero further dilution) to be close to certain.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report share-based payment note (Extracted/RUA.NZ_Annual_FY2025.txt:3212, $41,782); H1 FY2026 SBC $69,625
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted = 339.402m ordinary (Aug-2026, post warrant/share activity per H1 FY2026 note and subsequent-events disclosure) + 8.733m warrants at NZ$0.015 strike, all in the money at NZ$0.035. Share count is NOT held flat: dilution here is genuine non-SBC rescue issuance, not grant dilution. Base case models one further NZ$3.5m net raise at NZ$0.025 (+140m shares -> 488.1m); bear recap branch models NZ$3.0m at NZ$0.012 (+250m -> 598.1m); bull assumes no further raise. Shares more than doubled in 18 months (159.75m Jun-2024 -> 338.04m Dec-2025), so modelling zero further dilution in base/bear would not be conservative - it would be wrong.
inputs.balance_sheet_staleness_note: Cash NZ$2.166m / borrowings NZ$1.813m are the 31-Dec-2025 interim balance sheet - 8 months stale at valuation date. At the H1 burn rate (~NZ$1.52m/half) cash today is likely materially lower absent the facility sale settling or a further raise; net cash of +NZ$0.353m should be treated as approximately zero. The FY2026 annual report (due ~Sep/Oct 2026) is the refresh trigger.
inputs.notes: Model: probability-weighted scenario model on forward EV/Sales, per the dcf-methods routing for a name straddling distressed and operating-company rows. Owner-FCF DCF rejected (no positive FCF in any period on record); NTA/book models rejected (two consecutive disclaimers of opinion make the balance sheet non-audit-assured); receivership waterfall rejected (going-concern basis, real growing revenue). First valuation of this ticker - no MEMORY.md entry existed. Filings are in whole NZD; CSV in millions; EPS in dollars.

wacc_rationale: 28% NZD cost of equity, built from the flows' own currency: NZ 10-yr risk-free ~4.5% + NZ equity risk premium ~5% x beta ~1.2 -> ~10.5-11.5% NZ micro-cap base. Explicit premiums stacked on top: (a) +5% illiquidity - sub-NZ$15m market cap trading at a tick floor where one NZ$0.005 tick is 14% of the price, thin turnover; (b) +4% information quality - two consecutive disclaimers of opinion mean forecasts and the balance sheet carry auditor-unverifiable risk beyond normal micro-cap opacity; (c) +4% customer and geographic concentration - Australia ~50% of H1 FY2026 revenue under a live TGA prescribing review, one distribution partner per market, German prices compressing toward EUR4/gram; (d) +3% pre-profitability execution risk on an unproven asset-light pivot. Total ~27.5-28.5%, rounded to 28%. DOUBLE-CHARGE AVOIDANCE, stated explicitly: insolvency/going-concern failure risk is deliberately EXCLUDED from this rate. It is priced once, as the 60% insolvency branch inside the 40%-weighted bear scenario. The 28% rate covers only the surviving-company risks (illiquidity, information quality, concentration, execution). The same rate is used for all three scenarios - no per-scenario WACC differences, per the charge-risk-once rule.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs are unusable as forward anchors. Revenue 3yr CAGR of 297% is off a near-zero FY2022 base (NZ$0.024m) and describes the abandoned owned-cultivation era plus the pivot, not a repeatable rate. Equity CAGR is deeply negative (-41%/yr over 3yr) because ~NZ$8.5m of goodwill/PP&E was impaired in FY2024 - it measures capital destruction, not compounding. FCF and EPS CAGRs are undefined (negative in every period). The selected 46.4% is the BASE scenario's forward revenue CAGR (NZ$2.8m FY2026E -> NZ$6.0m FY2028E), used as the screener's forward-growth proxy.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) is negative in every year FY2020-FY2026H1; adjusted CAGRs are as undefined as reported ones.

base.narrative: Revenue compounds off the H1 FY2026 run-rate (NZ$1.334m half, +92% YoY): FY2026E NZ$2.8m -> FY2027E NZ$4.5m (UK deal contributes partially, below its NZ$5m/yr stated average, plus Australia/NZ/Germany growth) -> FY2028E NZ$6.0m. The Gisborne facility sells near carrying value (~NZ$0.7m net to the group after retiring the secured building loan), but cumulative burn to breakeven (~NZ$4.6m from Dec-2025) still exceeds resources, so ONE further dilutive raise is modelled: NZ$3.5m net at NZ$0.025 (consistent with the Nov-2024 rights price of $0.025 and the ~annual raise cadence), +140m shares -> 488.1m diluted. Exit at 1.5x FY2028E sales - a multiple for a sub-scale, roughly-breakeven, going-concern-qualified distributor with no cost moat, NOT a profitable branded-pharma multiple. Net cash at exit ~0 (raise proceeds largely consumed by remaining burn).

bull.narrative: The July-2026 UK deal converts broadly as announced (~NZ$5m/yr from FY2027), Germany holds despite EUR4/gram price compression, the Australian TGA review does not close the clinic/telehealth channel: FY2026E NZ$2.9m -> FY2027E NZ$7.0m -> FY2028E NZ$10.5m. Operating breakeven is reached during FY2027; cash NZ$2.17m + facility sale ~NZ$0.7m net + NZ$0.13m warrant exercise proceeds bridge the remaining burn WITHOUT a further raise, so dilution stops at today's 348.1m fully diluted. Exit at 2.5x FY2028E sales - a growing, breakeven exporter with proven multi-market contracts - with ~NZ$1.2m net cash. This is the scenario the current NZ$0.035 price is closest to pricing.

bear.narrative: Revenue growth stalls: the TGA review compresses the Australian channel (~50% of H1 FY2026 revenue), German price compression squeezes a cost-disadvantaged outsourced producer, the UK deal underdelivers (undisclosed partner, unaudited forward figure, and Rua's own liquidity constrains supply). The facility sale disappoints or is delayed - it has been 'in progress' across multiple periods without completion. With ~7 months of runway (NZ$2.17m cash vs NZ$1.52m/half burn, both figures 8 months stale), the company hits the wall. Two branches: 60% insolvency/fire-sale wind-down - equity ~NZ$0 (verified-tangible assets ~NZ$2.8m less NZ$1.8m borrowings less wind-down costs leaves nothing meaningful; goodwill worth zero in a wind-down); 40% punitive recapitalisation - NZ$3.0m at NZ$0.012 (below the NZ$0.015 warrant strike, consistent with the 47.9%-discount Nov-2024 rights precedent), +250m shares -> 598.1m diluted, revenue flat ~NZ$2.5m, exit 0.6x sales -> NZ$0.002/share. Blended bear IV: NZ$0.0008 - near-total loss.

bear.implied_exit_multiple_basis: EV/Sales on FY2028E revenue, recap branch only; insolvency branch is 0

valuation.notes: terminal_pct_of_value is 100% by construction - all value in this model is the discounted exit value; there are no positive interim flows to collect. street = house in every scenario: the model is not FCF-based so the SBC accounting-regime band does not operate; SBC (~NZ$0.07m/half) is trivial next to the modelled rescue-raise dilution, which is charged explicitly through scenario share counts.

entry_price.method: Repo-standard semantics adapted to the scenario-multiple model: entry price = price at which the scenario's exit equity value, discounted at the 15% hurdle instead of the 28% cost of equity, is recovered per (scenario-diluted) share. No interim distributions exist to add. NOTE: the weighted entry price (NZ$0.0179) sits ABOVE the weighted IV (NZ$0.0145) - expected and correct here, because the 15% hurdle is far below the 28% risk-appropriate discount rate. The IV answers 'what is it worth at a rate that prices the surviving-company risks'; the entry price answers 'what could you pay and still make 15% in expectation'. Both are less than half the current NZ$0.035 price.

required_return_table.note: 28% row is the model's own cost of equity. Even at a 9% required return the base case is worth NZ$0.0155 - less than half the current price. The current price is not explicable by discount-rate choice; it requires the bull revenue/multiple path.

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows: cost of equity (%). Columns: exit EV/Sales multiple on FY2028E base-case revenue of NZ$6.0m, net cash 0, 488.1m diluted shares. Replaces the WACC x terminal-growth grid, which does not exist in a multiple-exit model.
sensitivity.reading: No cell in the grid reaches the current NZ$0.035 price - not even 2.5x sales at a 20% discount rate on today-ish dilution assumptions. Reaching NZ$0.035 on base-case revenue requires ~4.5x forward sales, i.e. the multiple the market currently pays on the run-rate.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 40% (vs 15% house default): two CONSECUTIVE disclaimers of opinion - the most severe audit outcome available - plus an explicit going-concern material uncertainty conditional on two things outside company control (revenue forecasts the auditor twice could not corroborate, and a facility sale 'in progress' across multiple periods without completion), against ~7 months of runway on 8-month-stale figures. This sits mid-range of the 35-45% the situation warrants. Bull 20% (vs 35% default): the UK deal is signed but with an undisclosed partner and an unaudited forward figure, the company has a history of announced opportunities not converting, and the bull case needs three independent things to go right simultaneously (UK converts, Germany holds through EUR4/gram compression, TGA review spares the Australian channel) plus zero further dilution. Base 40% carries the remainder. Weights sum to 1.0.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position null: house and street coincide because the model is multiple-based, not FCF-based - the SBC accounting-regime band does not operate. Dilution risk is charged through explicit scenario share counts instead.
probability_weighted.verdict: Weighted IV NZ$0.0145 is ~59% BELOW the current NZ$0.035 price. Stated plainly: at these weights the stock is materially overvalued. The current price is approximately the probability-weighted value you would get with weights of roughly bear 10% / base 25% / bull 65% - i.e. the market is treating the UK deal as largely delivered and further dilution as unlikely, neither of which the filings support yet. No buy signal has been reverse-engineered: the honest answer is below the price.

sanity_check.pe_check: SKIPPED deliberately - Rua has never reported a profit in any period on record (FY2020-H1 FY2026 all losses); no P/E history exists to trip against.
sanity_check.pb_check: SKIPPED deliberately as a primary anchor - the FY2024 and FY2025 accounts both carry a disclaimer of opinion citing recoverability of ~NZ$5.3m of goodwill/PP&E/held-for-sale assets, so the NZ$5.845m book equity is not audit-assured. Memo only: verified-tangible equity ~NZ$2.8m (equity less NZ$2.195m goodwill less NZ$0.861m held-for-sale facility) = ~NZ$0.008/share on today's diluted count - which brackets the base-case IV of NZ$0.0113 from below and is itself ~77% below the market price.
sanity_check.ev_sales_anchor: Current EV NZ$11.53m (339.4m x NZ$0.035 = NZ$11.88m market cap, less NZ$0.35m net cash) = 4.3x annualised H1 FY2026 run-rate sales (NZ$2.67m) and 7.6x FY2025 sales. The model's exit multiples (bear 0.6x / base 1.5x / bull 2.5x FORWARD FY2028E sales) are all below what the market pays today on trailing/run-rate sales - the model assumes multiple COMPRESSION from the current price, not expansion, which is the conservative direction. Rua's own EV/Sales history is unusable as a band (EV was 5-10x higher against near-zero revenue in FY2021-FY2023). Internal consistency passes; the gap to the market price is the finding, not a model failure.
sanity_check.notes: passed=true means the model is internally consistent and anchored; it does NOT mean the stock passes a value screen - weighted IV is 59% below price.

in_the_discount_rate: customer/geographic concentration (AU ~50%, single partner per market)
in_the_flows: German price compression and TGA review (bear revenue path)
UK deal conversion risk (base < deal run-rate; only bull assumes full conversion)
risks_priced.double_charge_avoidance: Each risk appears in exactly one bucket; same 28% rate across all scenarios.
